minutes_text:
PARKING & TRAFFIC COMMISSION
  City of Inglewood City Hall Community Room A
  One West Manchester Blvd.Inglewood, CA 90301
  JULY 2021 MEETING MINUTES
1. Roll Call
a. A meeting was held at the City of Inglewood located on the 1st Floor in Conference Room A at 7:12 pm.
b. Attendees included:
  1. Michael Benbow, Chairperson
  2. Charles Braggs, District 1
  3. Leonel Garcia, District 2
  4. Barbara Brooks, District 4
  5. Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3
  6. Sergeant Freeman Smith Jr, Traffic Unit Commander
  7. Peter Puglese, City Traffic Engineer
  8. Raquel Méndez, Associate Engineer

2. Approval of Minutes
a. None

3. Public Comments
a. A resident from District 4 inquired about neighborhood parking and the Citywide Parking Permit
  Program. The residents' concerns were that the program is unfair, costly, and not enough is applied to
  protect residents' privacy. City staff provided background information on the program and explained how
  to initiate an amendment to the program. It was reported that the main corridors do not have a parking
  permit restriction.

b. Another issue discussed was the vehicle's speed and racing on the north side of 118th Street and Crenshaw
  Boulevard in the late hours of the day. Unfortunately, it isn't easy to monitor and track such cases. The
  Commander of the Traffic Unit informed the resident that the City had developed a unit to handle these
  types of cases. California Highway Patrol and the City of Inglewood are on board to avoid speeding.
  The dispatch enforcement phone line; (310) 412-8732, was given for the resident to contact and report
  from a vehicle parked in the alley during the sweeping time to unsafe speed vehicles.

c. Excessive red curbs on Evergreen Street is another topic discussed. City staff provided information on
  the justification of the need for red curbs. The determining factor depends on the sight distance for the
  vehicle to turn, the location of a fire hydrant, the opening of the catch basin, the tips of the ends of the
  driveways, the curb is less than 20 feet long between the driveways, and will there be enough space for
  emergency vehicles to park. The resident was recommended to contact the Department of Public Works
  for a field inspection evaluation since it is a case-by-case scenario.
